hooks.command: jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // ""' | grep -Eq '\.claude/projects/.*/memory/' && { echo 'BLOCKED: the built-in memory is forbidden in this repo entirely, not by category (AGENTS.md, Persistence rules). Route the fact instead: a repo convention or a fact about the code -> AGENTS.md; work state, a decision, an open question -> a vimarsha in r5; a fact about the user that no project owns -> the personal realm @<handle>/mind (minding skill). This dir stays frozen at its prohibition stub.' >&2; exit 2; } || exit 0

echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"Orient in NKS before acting (skill verstak:entry): nks_orient(realm=\"r5\", focus=\"844\") — read the ACTIVE BIANHUA map. Then open your agenda: nks_orient(realm=\"r5\", focus=\"931\") — incoming posed_to vimarshas are this session inbox; pick up or explicitly defer each before starting repo work. The built-in memory is forbidden here entirely — see AGENTS.md, Persistence rules."}}'

IN=$(cat); [ "$(echo "$IN" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false')" = "true" ] && exit 0; T=$(echo "$IN" | jq -r '.transcript_path // ""'); [ -f "$T" ] || exit 0; tail -n 80 "$T" | grep -q '"type":"tool_use"' && exit 0; tail -n 5 "$T" | grep -q '?' && exit 0; echo 'BLOCKED: this turn ends without a change and without a question. Announcing what you are about to do ends you — no input is due, and nothing wakes you until someone pings. Do the thing, or ask the question where its addressee will find it (the user here, a posed_to vimarsha for another doer). What you are on belongs in the occupation line on your channel, not in a turn that stops.' >&2; exit 2

jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""' | grep -q 'git push' && echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":"A push landed — first ask which kind. Done here is merged to main, so a push that merely opens or updates a PR ships nothing: record an answer with addressed_by where one genuinely stands, but leave node bodies and modes describing the method main actually carries — a model written ahead of the merge describes something the repo does not have, and a withdrawn PR leaves it lying. After a merge: update NKS (r5, #844) from fresh artifact evidence, never from intent — advance the bianhua map; end by axis what the merge settled (addressed_by records the answer, release is its own volitional act); walk the whole shipped contour, but flip a mode only where the evidence covers it, since a mode flip is itself a claim; work the #931 inbox. Re-read the diff and the nodes for borrowed project-management words (ticket, backlog, sprint, epic, story, done, blocker, committed): name each one to the user and ask what this project calls it, instead of swapping it yourself."}}' || true
